issues.title: Keyspace setup failure logged at DEBUG instead of previous WARN
issues.verdictReason: Confirmed: pre-PR code in start_setting_keyspace_for_connection logged the failure via warn! (and, worse, still returned Ok so the broken connection was silently pooled). The PR now correctly discards the connection via Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace) in handle_ready_connection (connection_pool.rs:897-909), but the per-attempt message there is debug!, and when the pool is non-empty update_shared_conns is skipped, so repeated keyspace failures on a partially-healthy pool are now invisible above debug level where before they were WARN.
issues.scopeReason: The log-level and visibility change is part of this PR's own refactor of keyspace-failure handling, and the same diff also fixes a worse pre-existing bug (silently pooling a connection with the wrong keyspace), so the behavior change is intentional but its observability side-effect should be reconsidered as part of this change.

reportedAs.code-review-ad: Failed initialization USE requests previously logged at WARN and now log at DEBUG. When existing connections remain, the error also stays out of shared pool state. At INFO/WARN, repeated refill failures therefore become invisible to callers and operators.

issues.title: New keyspace regression test awaits ready_connections.next() with no timeout
issues.verdictReason: Confirmed both `let event = refiller.ready_connections.next().await.unwrap();` calls (lines 1634 and 1667) are unguarded awaits on a keyspace USE request completing through the mocked proxy; if that future never resolves the test hangs indefinitely under plain `cargo test`. This pattern (bare .next().await in a test) does not exist anywhere in main's version of this file, and the same PR demonstrates awareness of the risk by wrapping a different new test's wait in tokio::time::timeout (line 2001), making the omission here inconsistent with the PR's own precedent.
issues.scopeReason: The test and both unbounded awaits are new code added by this PR.

reportedAs.code-review-ad: Both new waits (lines 1634 and 1667) depend on a keyspace request without a local timeout. If that operation stalls, the test cannot reach its assertions or explicit proxy shutdown. Nextest supplies an external 120-second deadline, but the PR's documented cargo test invocation does not; the production timeout omission predates this PR.

issues.title: New keyspace-failure tests omit CONTRIBUTING.md-required setup_tracing() call
issues.verdictReason: Verified: CONTRIBUTING.md:92 states 'any new tests should' call setup_tracing() so tracing output is visible on failure. keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill (line 1474) and keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state (line 1526) do not call it, while this same PR's other new tests (resharding_discards_old_connections_and_balances_metrics, excess_connection_limit_clears_connections_and_balances_metrics, full_pool_clears_excess_connections_and_balances_metrics) do call setup_tracing() at lines 1728, 1869, 1973 respectively.
issues.scopeReason: Both tests are newly added by this PR and the convention is self-evidently followed elsewhere in the same diff.

reportedAs.code-review-ad: Neither new test (lines 1474 and 1526) calls setup_tracing(), despite CONTRIBUTING.md:92 directing new tests to do so. Isolated failures can consequently omit the required diagnostic tracing. The PR documents no exception.
